correctness.rationale: For each integer \(k\ge1\), direct reduction modulo five proves depths \(0,1,2\) by residue class. Hensel lifts establish permutations on the two periodic disks. The integral-polynomial iterate-lifting lemma is proved by a first-order Taylor congruence and yields the exact periods and hence 3k-1 cycles. Normalized Legendre characters separate the two near-two cycles; inverse quadratic congruences give precisely one transient predecessor per periodic vertex and either 0, \(2\cdot5^{t/2}\), or \(5^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}\) further leaves. Every depth-two vertex has indegree zero. The independently implemented complete finite directed graphs \(1\le k\le7\), 97655 states, match the proof, but are not offered as its universal justification.

originality.rationale: The final claim is the exact cycle-by-cycle distribution of all transient depth-two branches and resulting rooted component sizes, not the already-known periodic-point spectrum. Gassert classifies Chebyshev maps over finite fields, not the rings \(\mathbb Z/5^k\mathbb Z\). Li--Lu--Tan--Chen classify permutation Chebyshev maps, and this quadratic is noninjective modulo five. Panraksa--Tangboonduangjit classify exact periods for all odd prime-power rings but explicitly distinguish the transient-tree problem as separate (conclusion). The new quadratic-sign selection of precisely one cycle at even levels is not implied by a cycle census. Actual topical index and literature queries did not identify equivalent branch incidence; this is a best-knowledge assessment with residual risk.
residual_risks: A more specialized or unlocated published graph computation could already give the same five-adic depth-two branch incidence.
The cycle counts are already covered by broader exact-period theorems; only the critical-tree attachment law and resulting full components are assessed as original.

value.rationale: Character-selected critical branches are a natural, mathematically distinct invariant beyond known Chebyshev cycle length counts. An infinite tower of residue-ring graphs has complete branch positions and nonuniform exact fiber sizes, concentrated on precisely one of two equal-length cycles at each even valuation. This resolves a substantive case of the separately identified nonpermuting incoming-tree problem and permits exact component-size calculations at arbitrary precision; it is not a parameter substitution into the known periodic census.
